Light: Blue dusk light from the city through the glass wall, plus warm interior light on the floor and a few ceiling lights reflected in the glass. The artwork: The building has been turned into a greenhouse: steam mists the windows and a reflective pond holds giant water lilies under grow lights. Materials: water lilies, pond liner, steam and grow lights. Framing: Frontal, symmetrical view at standing height, normal lens, centred on the glass wall; the work stands on the floor across the lower middle and fills about 85 percent of the frame width; the glass wall fills the upper two thirds. Horizontal 3:2 frame. No people in the room. Colour and exposure: Dim, cool, strong saturated blue from outside, warm wood tones on the floor, medium contrast. Style: a real photograph by a professional exhibition photographer, high detail, the kind of image published on Contemporary Art Daily or a museum press page. Unremarkable and credible. Not cinematic: no dramatic spotlight, no lens flare, no haze unless the artwork makes it, no vignette. No legible text on the artwork; wall labels are small and not readable. No watermark.
